title: Couple Dolphins things to keep in mind as we approach 6 p.m. Sunday cut-down to 53: 1). You can put 2 players on IR as you cut to 53 (meaning you're essentially keeping 55). Those players can return after 4 weeks. Trey Moore likely will be one. If there's another, Kenneth Grant would be an option. We'll see. 2). Dolphins are 11th in waiver order claim for players cut with less than 4 years experience. The waiver claim process is midday Monday. 3). Dolphins can move Storm Duck and Darrell Baker from active PUP to reserve PUP on Sunday; they don't count toward 53. Under new rule, players on reserve PUP can begin practicing after team's first 2 games, down from 4.
summary:
Couple Dolphins things to keep in mind as we approach 6 p.m. Sunday cut-down to 53: 
1). You can put 2 players on IR as you cut to 53 (meaning you're essentially keeping 55). Those players can return after 4 weeks. Trey Moore likely will be one. If there's another, Kenneth Grant would be an option. We'll see.
2). Dolphins are 11th in waiver order claim for players cut with less than 4 years experience. The waiver claim process is midday Monday.
3). Dolphins can move Storm Duck and Darrell Baker from active PUP to reserve PUP on Sunday; they don't count toward 53. Under new rule, players on reserve PUP can begin practicing after team's first 2 games, down from 4.

3). Dolphins can move Storm Duck and Darrell Baker from active PUP to reserve PUP on Sunday; they don't count toward 53. Under new rule, players on reserve PUP can begin practicing after team's first 2 games, down from 4.

title: The new practice squad rules have been beneficial to teams, but they've made roster projections much tougher. It used to be simple: If you cut a vet, he was gone. Now you can get them to the practice squad and even promise elevations so they don't lose anything financially. There's also roster gymnastics like the Korie Black move last year when the Giants carried him on the initial 53 and then tried to slide him to the practice squad the next day after making some waiver claims. There's risk involved, as Black left for the Jets' PS (before eventually returning). But it's a crafty strategy because most teams make their waiver claims in the initial rush when there are hundreds of players available after cut day. They may be less inclined to make a claim in a day or two when their roster is more settled. I wonder if you see a move like that to try to protect someone like Thomas Fidone or Bobby Jamison-Travis. The lock of all locks is that the Giants will make at least one addition to their D-line between now and the opener. Depending on the severity of his groin injury, Black could be a candidate for the new rule that allows players to be designated to return from IR on cut day. That would allow the Giants to keep a promising young player without exposing him to other teams

And I think that I would be remiss if I didn't say how proud I am of Tyler and how hard he's worked.”

title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer On the quarterback situation: “I mean, it's neck and neck and love both those guys. They're both great competitors. What I love about them both is both guys want to win the spot. Both guys want to compete, but both guys are really happy for each other when they do well. That was last week, Sam cheering on Joe, Joe cheering on Sam in this game. That's the tough part of this weekend because I am really proud of this team and how much we've accomplished over the past seven, eight weeks. And the human element of this is hard. We’ve got a lot of really good football players and it's hard to keep them all. You can't unfortunately keep them all, but we'll get a little bit of sleep tonight, get in tomorrow and start making some tough decisions. On the measurables of the quarterbacks: "We're looking at everything. I think all the things that you're identifying are real. I think we're looking at everything. We chart every pass in training camp. We chart obviously the stats from the preseason games, all the decisions that they make in the run game. What you’ve got to remember is part of the deal is how you handle the run game checks and things like that. We're a volume based offense and it really is a true battle. We've got some tough decisions coming up.”
